description: An incorrect validation DOMAIN/SCOPE permanently or indefinitely bricks a user-facing path: a global counter checked against a local/per-generation/per-user limit (or a wrong validation domain) blocks an intended mint/claim/withdraw/settle/forge/buy/sell action, or prevents a lifecycle phase from completing. Anchored on TraitForge 2024-07 H-01 (mintWithBudget loop guard `_tokenIds < maxTokensPerGen` uses the global token id vs the per-generation cap, bricking budget-minting from generation 2 onward).

poc_level_descriptors.L3A: show the validation uses the wrong domain (global counter vs per-scope limit / wrong validation set)
poc_level_descriptors.L3B: drive the system to the boundary where the wrong-scope check trips and assert the user-facing path (mint/claim/withdraw/settle/forge/buy/sell) is blocked for a normal user
poc_level_descriptors.L3C: assert the brick is permanent/indefinite (no setter / no self-recovery; recovers only via privileged intervention, migration, or upgrade) and that it affects a core phase or many/all users

high_severity_rationale: High requires proving the wrong-scope validation PERMANENTLY/indefinitely bricks a CORE user-facing path for many/all users with no self-recovery (recovers only via privileged intervention / migration / upgrade). Medium is proven by showing the validation scope is wrong and a user-facing path is materially blocked, without a permanence + core/all-users proof. This is a LIVENESS / denial-of-asset-movement class -> per the P88 severity gate it must NOT be under-rated below Medium when source-backed; it is NOT a bounded/lazy accounting issue.
negative_control_template: Replace the wrong-domain check with the correct scope (e.g. `generationMintCounts[currentGeneration] < maxTokensPerGen` instead of `_tokenIds < maxTokensPerGen`, or the per-user/per-scope counter). Assert the user-facing path works again at and beyond the boundary, with no other change.
